drhp.business: Ishan is engaged in marketing/selling projects that supply machines, erection/installation, commissioning and operational training for sugar plants, hydro power plants and pollution control systems. It also provides high-end engineering services and solutions across Hydro Power, Sugar & Pollution Control Systems, and derives a significant proportion of its business from exports.
drhp.end_markets: ASEAN countries|Vietnam|Southeast Asia|Africa (diversification target)|North America (diversification target)
drhp.expansion: Ishan has, since 2005, promoted over 40 Hydro Power Projects (1 MW–60 MW) across ASEAN countries, with an established presence in Vietnam and Southeast Asia. The Company continues to focus on exporting Sugar Machinery and related equipment to ASEAN countries while pursuing diversification into new geographies including Africa and North America, and continues to strengthen its presence in pollution control and clean energy technologies. The Company operates in the service sector with no manufacturing activities and states that no capital investment was required or incurred during the year on energy conservation equipment.

litigation.note: Secretarial Audit notes SEBI sent a communication/mail regarding investigation/information requirements (Company replied) and NSE sought clarification on utilisation of IPO proceeds (Company replied); no penalty was imposed by SEBI or NSE during the year; no significant/material order was passed by regulators, courts or tribunals affecting going concern.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- India's engineering goods exports rose to approximately US$122.43 billion in FY2025-26, the third consecutive year of record performance, supported by Government initiatives (MAI Scheme, PLI Scheme, Export Promotion Mission).
- Demand in the engineering sector continues to be driven by capacity expansion in infrastructure, power, renewable energy, mining, oil & gas, refineries, steel, automobiles and consumer durables.
- Growing emphasis on Renewable Energy and Pollution Control is expected to sustain global demand for the equipment and engineering services the Company specialises in.
- The decline in revenue for the year is attributed to a large one-off bulk supply arrangement with a domestic customer that was executed and fully completed in FY2024-25 and did not recur to the same extent in the year under review.
- Exporters continue to navigate global headwinds including tariff actions by key markets such as the USA and volatility in global demand.

capex_expansion.body: Ishan has, since 2005, promoted over 40 Hydro Power Projects (1 MW–60 MW) across ASEAN countries, with an established presence in Vietnam and Southeast Asia. The Company continues to focus on exporting Sugar Machinery and related equipment to ASEAN countries while pursuing diversification into new geographies including Africa and North America, and continues to strengthen its presence in pollution control and clean energy technologies. The Company operates in the service sector with no manufacturing activities and states that no capital investment was required or incurred during the year on energy conservation equipment.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- SWOT flags concentration of revenue in a limited number of large-value orders as leading to year-on-year revenue volatility; management explicitly names this as the concentration risk it is trying to diversify away from.
- Volatility in order inflows is flagged as a threat affecting revenue predictability.
- The Company derives a significant proportion of its business from exports and remains exposed to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates.
- Exporters continue to navigate global headwinds including tariff actions by key markets such as the USA and volatility in global demand.
- SWOT threats list payments from buyers getting delayed.
- SWOT threats cite competition from established global and domestic players.
- Statutory Auditor's Emphasis of Matter notes the Company is yet to complete formalities of seeking extension of time from the RBI for delay in recovery of dues from foreign customers outstanding beyond 270 days; the Company also wrote off export receivables during the year and provided for Expected Credit Loss.
- SWOT weaknesses note new suppliers of Hydro Power plants, with no projects to showcase in Vietnam as of now, despite the Company's stated established presence there.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to focus on export of Sugar Machinery and related equipment to ASEAN countries, while pursuing diversification into new geographies including Africa and North America.
- Continue to strengthen presence in pollution control and clean energy technologies.
- Reinvest earnings to support long-term objectives and reinforce market position rather than distribute a dividend, given the ongoing need for funds to support business growth and expansion.
- Work towards diversifying the order book across geographies and customers to address concentration risk from a limited number of large-value orders.
